Chief_Complaint.content: Right knee pain with clicking after increased running
Chief_Complaint.source_text: R knee pain w/ clicking after increased running

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Approximately 2 weeks of right knee pain and clicking after overdoing workouts
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • ~2 wks R knee pain + clicking after “overdoing workouts”

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient is training for a marathon in June and started a running program about 1 month ago, running up to 7–8 miles
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • Training for marathon in June; started running program ~1 mo ago; runs up to 7–8 miles

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Right knee pain begins about 20 minutes into a run (approximately 2.5–3 miles) and has been worsening to the point that the patient stopped running last time
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • Pain begins ~20 min into run (~2.5–3 miles); worsening → stopped running last time

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Right knee clicking is noted especially with knee flexion and extension during abdominal exercises
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • Clicking noted esp w/ knee flexion/extension during ab exercises

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Right knee pain is located in the middle of the knee, sometimes slightly to the right side
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • Pain location: “middle” of knee, sometimes slightly to R side

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Mild right knee swelling occurred after the first run and improved with ice
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • Swelling: mild after first run; improved w/ ice

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Right knee is not currently swollen and there is no pain at rest currently
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • Swelling: mild after first run; improved w/ ice; not swollen currently; no pain at rest currently

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient reports right knee instability or giving way is not bad and that it mainly hurts
Patient denies right knee locking or inability to straighten
Patient has no issues with stairs
Patient has no issues with walking
Patient is able to fully extend and flex the right knee
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • ROM: able to fully extend and flex

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Single episode of tingling in the right toes after a run which resolved, with no persistent numbness or tingling
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • Single episode tingling R toes after run; resolved; no persistent numbness/tingling

History_of_Present_Illness.content: No color or temperature change in the lower legs reported
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • No color/temperature change in lower legs

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Occasional sock-line indentations after standing a long time, consistent with dependent swelling
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: • Occasional sock-line indentations after standing long time (dependent swelling)

Past_Medical_History.content: History of prior severe urinary tract infection requiring emergency room visit with initial concern for kidney stones
Past_Medical_History.source_text: • Prior severe UTI (ER visit; initially concern for kidney stones)

Medications.content: Ibuprofen up to 400 mg as needed

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is training for a marathon and plays sports including ice hockey
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: • Training for marathon; plays sports incl ice hockey

Assessment.content: Right knee pain with exertion and clicking for 2 weeks in the setting of increased running with intermittent swelling after running, no locking or significant instability; concern for overuse injury versus internal derangement or cartilage issue
Assessment.source_text: 1. R knee pain w/ exertion + clicking x2 wks in setting of increased running; intermittent swelling after running; no locking/instability; concern for overuse injury vs internal derangement/cartilage issue.

Assessment.content: Transient tingling of the right toes after a run, single episode, resolved
Assessment.source_text: 2. Transient tingling R toes post-run (single episode), resolved.

Assessment.content: Intermittent dependent lower extremity swelling by history with sock indentations, without calf pain or color or temperature change
Assessment.source_text: 3. Intermittent dependent LE swelling by history (sock indentations), no calf pain/color/temp change.

Plan_of_Care.content: Continue RICE measures including frequent ice therapy for the right knee
Decrease and ease up on running and avoid running if pain is severe enough to stop
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Decrease/ease up on running; avoid running if pain severe enough to stop

Plan_of_Care.content: NSAIDs are acceptable, patient may use ibuprofen with food
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • NSAIDs: ok to use ibuprofen w/ food

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescribe a stronger anti-inflammatory medication to take regularly instead of ibuprofen and instruct not to combine them
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Rx stronger anti-inflammatory to take regularly instead of ibuprofen (do not combine)

Plan_of_Care.content: Refer patient to physiotherapy for full assessment and examination of the right knee
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Refer to physiotherapy for full assessment/exam

Plan_of_Care.content: Consider imaging of the right knee after examination if there is concern for cartilage or internal knee pathology
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Consider imaging after exam if concern for cartilage/internal knee pathology

Plan_of_Care.content: Offer in-clinic assessment if physiotherapy appointment is delayed too long
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • If physio appt delay too long, offer in-clinic assessment

Plan_of_Care.content: Advise patient to seek urgent care if persistent swelling, heat or redness, fever or feeling unwell, or if the knee locks up and cannot bend or straighten
Plan_of_Care.source_text: • Seek urgent care if persistent swelling, heat/redness, fever/feeling unwell, or knee locks up (can’t bend/straighten)

Physical_Findings.content: Visit conducted via video consultation with no physical exam findings documented
Physical_Findings.source_text: • Video consult; no exam findings documented

Physical_Findings.content: No current visible swelling of the right knee reported by the patient
Physical_Findings.source_text: • No current visible swelling reported by pt
